sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by her in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. Brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
That on 13-05-2024 at about 08.10 p.m, the petitioner was proceeding as a pedestrian to have a dinner at Hotel in Karapalli, Hosur, Krishnagiri Dist., when she reached opposite to GPT Petrol bunk, at that time rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.TN-70/S- 6584 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life came at high speed (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.3733/2024 and dashed the petitioner, as a result the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately she was shifted to Private Hospital, Hosur, for first aid, then she was shifted to Kempegowda Hospital, Bengaluru wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and incurred more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation,
medication, nourishment, attendant and other incidental charges.

It is contended that prior to the accident she was working as a Tailor and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
due to accidental injuries she could not able to continue her work and hence sustained loss of income and suffering from permanent disability.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.TN-70/S-6584.
Hence, the Hosur Police have registered a criminal case in Cr.100/2024 for the offence punishable U/sec.279 & 337 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- to the petitioner together with interest and with costs.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and hence she was placed (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.3733/2024 exparte, as service held sufficient.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and has filed objections.
04. Respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner.
While admitting about issuance of insurance policy in respect of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.TN-70/S-6584 this respondent restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the policy.

It is further denied age,
avocation, income of the petitioner, manner of accident and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner.
The rider of the offending vehicle has no valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident, hence there is a clear violation of terms and conditions of the policy by the owner.

It is contended that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner herself and offending vehicle was not involved in the alleged accident and it was intentionally implicated in the case to get unlawful benefit from the Insurance Company and the compensation claimed is more excessive,

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor:-
ISSUES

1. Whether the petitioner is proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 13.05.2024 at about 8.10 p.m. on Hosuru to Rayakarapalli,
opposite to GPT petrol bunk, Krishnagiri district, due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing registration No.TN-70-S- 6584 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
2. Whether Respondent No.2 proves that accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner?
Hence, petition is not maintainable?
3. Whether respondent No.2 proves that rider of motor cycle was not having valid license?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
5.
What Order
or Award?
06. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3.
They got marked documents as Ex.P1 to 16 and closed her side evidence.
07. Inspite of granting sufficient time, the respondent No.2 did not adduce evidence on its behalf.
Hence evidence of respondent No.2 is taken as nil and posted for arguments.

08. Heard both sides and perused the materials available on record.
09.

My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-

These issues are interlinked and inter related to each other, hence these issues are taken for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts of the case.
11. Petitioner filed affidavit in lieu of examination in chief and got examined as PW.1.
In her affidavit, she has reiterated the entire petition averments of the petition.

Though, she has been (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.3733/2024 elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner that due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider, the accident took place and she has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has produced 11 documents.

On perusal of the police documents i.e., Ex.P1 - FIR and Ex.P1(a) Translated copy of FIR it discloses that a case has been registered at TIW - Hosur P.S. Krishnagiri Dist., against rider of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/sec.279 and 337 of IPC, on the basis of Complaint lodged by the husband of the petitioner.

It discloses that on the date, place and time of accident when the petitioner was walking on the road opposite to GPT Petrol bunk, to have dinner at a Hotel, Karapalli, Krishnagiri Dist., at that time rider of offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner and caused the accident.
Immediately she was shifted to Meera Hospital, for first aid, then she was shifted to Kempegowda Hospital, Bengaluru for higher treatment.
Though the respondent no.2 counsel argued that there is a delay in lodging the complaint, in the complaint the husband of the petitioner has clearly explained about delay in lodging the complaint.

Ex.P3 is the IMV report which (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.3733/2024 disclose the date, Place and involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and it is opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defect in the vehicle.

Ex.P4 is the wound certificate it discloses that the petitioner has sustained one simple and one grievous injuries in a R.T.A. Further, the counsel for the respondent argued that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner herself.

Ex.P2 is the Spot sketch, Ex.P2(a) is the Translated copy of the spot sketch, it disclose that the accident occurred in the middle of the road when the petitioner was crossing the road in the highway.

sentences.text:
Though the counsel for respondent no.2 argued that the rider of offending vehicle had not possess valid and effective D.L. to ride the same as on the date of accident,
to disprove the said fact, neither the respondent no.2 got examined any evidence, nor produced any document on its behalf.
Further on perusal of charge sheet it does not contain the section for non possessing of D.L. by the rider of the offending vehicle.
Hence the said contention is not taken into consideration.
Therefore, by considering the materials available on record, it is clear that due to some contributory negligence on the part of the Petitioner this accident occurred.
Hence, some contributory negligence is taken on the part of the petitioner in the accident, but major negligence is taken on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, apportion of the negligence on the part of the petitioner is taken at 10% and 90% on the part of the rider of (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.3733/2024 the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, I have answered the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative, Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative and Issue No.3 in the Negative.

13. Issue No.4:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.
14.
To prove the age of the petitioner, she has not produced her birth certificate, School records or SSLC marks card to prove her exact date of birth.
However, she has produced Ex.P6 Notarized copy of her Aadhaar card.

Even though the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age for any person, but in the absence of any other documents, the same can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 07.08.1975 and the alleged accident occurred on 13.05.2024.
Therefore, considering the said document, this tribunal has taken the age of the petitioner as 49 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.3733/2024 multiplier applicable to the age group of 46 to 50 years is '13'.
15.

sentences.text: With regard to avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, she has not produced any document to that effect.

Therefore, in the absence of any such document, regarding her avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2024 to be taken as Rs.16,500/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has taken the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/-.
16.

According to the evidence of PW.3, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination affidavit that, petitioner has sustained:- Fracture Shaft of left Humerus.
Further deposed that recently on 17-06- 2025 he has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability purpose and the radiological examination shows, fracture united with implant in situ.
Further he has assessed permanent physical disability of about 32% of left upper limb and that of to the whole body at 11%.
He has produced OPD book and X-ray as per Ex.P15 and 16.
In the cross-examination PW.3/doctor (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.3733/2024 admits that he has not treated the petitioner personally and fracture are united.

However, by considering the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has considers functional disability of the petitioner at 10% to the whole body.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:

Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- The petitioner has produced Ex.P8 Discharge summary of KIMS hospital, it discloses that, she took treatment as inpatient in the said hospital from 14-05-2024 to 24-05-2024 and on 18-05-2024 she was undergone surgery, i.e.,
for 11 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.15,000/- under this head.
(SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.3733/2024 18. Pain and sufferings:-
As per Ex.P4 Wound certificate the petitioner has sustained sutured wound present over left occiput region and swelling and tenderness present over left upper arm.
The doctor has opined that the injury No.1 is simple and injury No.2 is grievous in nature.
Therefore, by considering the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner and opinion of the doctor, this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
19. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any document regarding her income and avocation and this tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.16,500/- p.m. and the petitioner was admitted in the hospital for 11 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of her stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out her avocation for atleast two months.

Thus,
taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.33,000/-
(Rs.16,500 x 2) under this head.
20. Medical expenses:-
The petitioner has produced Medical bills and some Prescriptions as per (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.3733/2024 Ex.P9 & 10 for Rs.3,12,804/-.
On perusal of Sl.No.3 of said medical bill, it is not in the name of the petitioner, hence, said bill is not taken into consideration.
To disprove the medical bills, the respondents have not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,12,548/- under this head.

21. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in her future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
22. Future medical expenses:-
According to doctor PW.3/doctor, the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants.
But he has not stated actual cost of the surgery and not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.
In the cross examination the doctor admitted that the fractures are united.

However, by considering the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner and evidence of the doctor, this tribunal awarded (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.3733/2024 reasonable compensation of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

As discussed in the Issue No.1 this tribunal already held that due to contributory negligence of the Petitioner and rider of the offending vehicle this accident occurred, hence the Petitioner's negligence part is taken at 10% and the rider of offending vehicle negligence is taken at 90%
respectively.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-
(SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.3733/2024 Rs.6,97,948/- - 69,794/- (10%) = Rs.6,28,154/-.
It is rounded off to Rs.6,28,200/-.

Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,28,200/-.
25.
Regarding liability:-
The respondent No.1 is the RC owner & respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent no.2 admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle and same was in force as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.

However, policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the primary liability is held on the respondent no.2, hence the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
26. Issue No.3:-

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

sentences.text: The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,28,200/- (Rupees six lakhs twenty eight thousand and two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner (as the petitioner is aged lady and she has incurred huge amount for her medication and also she has to incur some more amount towards her future medical expenses) through E-payment directly to her account on proper verification and identification of documents.
(SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.3733/2024 The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
